node.title: Replacing a module dependency
node.author: Bod
node.doctext:
We send automated emails with things like registration verifications automatically. We user [mod://MIME::Lite] to do the sending and use the default send mechanism which is sendmail as it is a Linux server.

But we are having some issues with deliverability. So, I decided to switch to using SMTP instead to see if that works more reliably. To send via SMTP [mod://MIME::Lite] uses [mod://Net::SMTP] which in turn requires [mod://MIME::Base64]. This last module is XS and I don't have it installed on the shared hosting.

We use [mod://Net::SMTP] elsewhere to send lots of emails so I have looked at what I did in the past to get around this problem. It turns out that I created a new module that inherits from [mod://Net::SMTP] and overrides the auth method. This works fine as we always send through the same SMTP server with the same authentication. Doing the same will be fine for the [mod://MIME::Lite] setup.

Like this: package Mail::SMTP; require Net::SMTP; $VERSION="1.0"; @ISA=qw(Net::SMTP); sub auth { my $self = shift; my $code; my $CMD_MORE = 3; my $CMD_OK = 2; my @cmd = ("AUTH LOGIN"); push @cmd, 'xxxxx='; # Base64 encoded username while (($code = $self->command(@cmd)->response()) == $CMD_MORE) { @cmd = ('xxxxx='); # Base64 encoded password } $code == $CMD_OK; } 1;

But, how can I easily get [mod://MIME::Lite] to use the new module inherited from [mod://New::SMTP]?

I could created a new module that inherits from [mod://MIME::Lite] and just override the send_by_smtp with the only change being the require file it calls. But that doesn't seen a very elegant solution!

Is there some way to instead put a new version of [mod://Net::SMTP] in a directory relative to my script and get [mod://MIME::Lite] to use that? If so, how can I inherit from a module of the same name (but a different path) as the new module?

Or is there a 'better' solution I am missing?
